title: Bounded above acyclic complexes compute a left derived functor
statement: Let $\mathcal A,\mathcal B$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], and assume $\mathcal A$ has enough projectives: every object admits an epimorphism from an object $P$ for which every map $P\to Y$ lifts across every epimorphism $X\to Y$. Every bounded above cochain complex $X$ has a quasi-isomorphism $P\to X$ with $P$ bounded above and each $P^i$ projective; when $X^i=0$ for $i>b$, one can require $P^i=0$ for $i>b$. Let $V:\mathcal A\to\mathcal B$ be additive and right exact (it preserves cokernels and finite direct sums), and suppose its total left derived functor $LV:D(\mathcal A)\to D(\mathcal B)$ exists, i.e. in Situation 05S8 of [def-pur-saturated-triangulated-localization], with the homotopy category $K(\mathcal A)$, its quasi-isomorphisms and the functor $Q\circ V$, the left derived functor is defined at every object, with canonical comparison $\varepsilon_C:LV(QC)\to Q(V(C))$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For every bounded above complex of projective objects $P$, $\varepsilon_P$ is an isomorphism. Call an object $A$ left $V$-acyclic when $\varepsilon_{A[0]}:LV(A[0])\to V(A)[0]$ is an isomorphism. For every bounded above complex $C$ of left $V$-acyclic objects, $\varepsilon_C$ is an isomorphism. Consequently, if $a:C\to X$ is a quasi-isomorphism with such $C$, the canonical identification of $LV(QX)$ with $Q(V(C))$ is $\varepsilon_C\circ LV(Qa)^{-1}$. These identifications are natural for maps between augmented resolutions: a square $a'f=ha$ gives $Q(V(f))\varepsilon_C LV(Qa)^{-1}=\varepsilon_{C'}LV(Qa')^{-1}LV(Qh)$.
